question_text: Why did William Jones feel the need to study Indian history, philosophy and law?
answer_text: William Jones felt the need to study Indian history, philosophy and law as this will not only help the British learn from Indian culture but it would also help Indian to rediscover their own heritage and understand the lost glories of their past. This would establish the British as guardians of Indian culture and gain total control.
final_answer: Thus, studying Indian culture was seen as a means to control and influence.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of historical context and implications.

chapter_name: civilising the native educating the nation
question_text: Why did James Mill and Thomas Macaulay think that European education was essential in India?
answer_text: James Mill and Thomas Macaulay thought that European education would enable Indians to recognize the advantages that flow from the expansion of trade and commerce and make them see the importance of developing the resources of the country. Introducing European ways of life would change their tastes and desires and create a demand for British goods, because Indians would begin to appreciate and buy things that were produced in Europe. It would also improve the moral character of Indians, making them truthful and honest, thus supplying the company with civil servants who could be trusted. Macaulay felt that knowledge of English would allow Indians to read some of the finest literature the world had produced and be aware of developments in Western Science and philosophy.
final_answer: Thus, they believed European education was crucial for economic and moral development.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves multi-step reasoning and understanding of colonial education policies.

question_text: Why did Mahatma Gandhi want to teach children handicrafts?
answer_text: Mahatma Gandhi wanted to teach children handicraft because that would develop their minds and their capacity to understand. This would also enable them to know how different things operated, helping them to have lived experience and practical knowledge.
final_answer: Thus, teaching handicrafts was seen as a way to enhance practical skills and understanding.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of Gandhi's educational philosophy.

subject: history
chapter_name: civilising the native educating the nation
question_text: Why did Mahatma Gandhi think that English education had enslaved Indians?
answer_text: English education, according to Mahatma Gandhi, created a sense of inferiority in the minds of Indians. It made them see Western civilisation as superior, and destroyed their pride in their own culture. Thus charmed by the West and by everything coming from the West, the Indians educated under the colonial system would end up being the admirers of Western culture.
final_answer: Thus, Gandhi believed English education led to cultural subjugation.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of cultural and psychological impacts of colonial education.
